newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Troll gas sales agreements come into force.
newsitem.headline: Norway Troll gas sales agreements come into force.

text.p: Norway's gas sales agreements from the giant Troll field came into force officially on Tuesday, securing gas exports for the next 20 years.

The field, Europe's largest offshore gas development, will send 90 million cubic metres per day of gas at its peak to the Kollsnes terminal on the west coast and on through several thousand kilometres of underwater pipeline southwards.
Norway's largest export contract ever is worth 700 billion crowns and will provide heat and lighting to 50 million people in Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria and Spain.
"Troll is the guarantor of supply security to Europe," said Trygve Skanding, spokesman for Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil).
"It's a huge development, it's safe and we now have flexibility."
While the contracts did not take effect officially until Tuesday, the Sleipner East gas field began deliveries under the agreements in 1993.
"Today the gas supplies began from Troll and Sleipner West," a Statoil statement said.
The combined deliveries will take Norway into the top five gas exporters in Europe along with Russia, the Netherlands, Algeria and Indonesia.
Norway, which is already the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia, will account for about 12 percent of gas supplies to Europe.
In Germany and France the Norwegian gas will obtain a market share of 30 and 37 percent respectively through the Troll contracts, Statoil said.
